prize_parts.citation: for showing how collateral constraints and balance-sheet frictions amplify and propagate shocks, generating credit cycles and shaping the role of financial intermediation in macroeconomic fluctuations

statement.case_for: Collateral constraints that tie borrowing to asset values give a tractable mechanism by which small shocks become large, persistent fluctuations (Kiyotaki-Moore 1997). This is a building block of modern macro-finance and of the models used to analyse financial crises and macroprudential policy. The core papers are close to thirty years old. They have been extended theoretically and empirically and were tested by the 2007-09 crisis, so there is no maturity concern. I moved from my opening two-name proposal to three names. The reason is that Gertler's contribution is not confined to the Bernanke-Gertler accelerator, which overlaps with the 2022 prize. His work with Kiyotaki on financial intermediation in macro models extends the collateral-constraint idea to banks and is a separate, later strand. Under that reading the three names credit one coherent discovery: financial frictions as an amplification mechanism in the macroeconomy.
statement.case_against: The 2022 prize on banks and financial crises is thematically adjacent, and a committee could judge that the field has recently been recognised. Part of Gertler's credit rests on the accelerator literature built with Bernanke, who is already a laureate, so the boundary between recognisable and already-recognised work is blurry. Gilchrist's empirical contribution is omitted under the three-name cap, and Gertler also appears on the New Keynesian ballot. Identification of the collateral channel in the data is mixed, and the evidence is more convincing for amplification in general than for the specific Kiyotaki-Moore mechanism.

responses.point: Krusell ranks B006 first with Kiyotaki, Moore and Gertler. He argues that the collateral-constraint mechanism and the financial-accelerator and intermediary tradition together became the standard way macro models credit and financial frictions, and that the post-2008 vindication settles timing. He flags the tension over crediting Gertler given Bernanke's earlier prize.
responses.response: I agree on maturity and on the centrality of the mechanism, and his point about the intermediary strand moves me to add Gertler. I would tie Gertler's credit to the intermediary-frictions work with Kiyotaki and to the quantitative financial-friction models. I would not tie it to the accelerator papers that overlap with Bernanke's 2022 recognition. I think the citation should say this explicitly, so that it does not look as if the prize re-recognises work already honoured. I do not accept that this fully dissolves the overlap concern. The committee should say openly that the accelerator credit is partly absorbed.

responses.point: Andersson ranks the BLP demand-estimation and dynamic-industry framework (B047) first. His argument is that it turned industrial organisation into a quantitative, policy-relevant field, with three decades of use in merger review, auctions and regulation, and that the Berry-Levinsohn-Pakes trio is a clean credit allocation.
responses.response: The methodological case is strong and the attribution is cleaner than in several other candidates. I did not rank B047 in my own top eight, so I cannot claim I have weighed it carefully against the macro-finance work. That absence reflects my limited expertise in structural industrial organisation, not a scientific judgement against it, and I would not want it read as one. Where I differ is on the common criterion of how much a discovery changed the way a whole field reasons. I still put collateral-based amplification slightly ahead, because it altered how macroeconomists model aggregate fluctuations and policy. The two prizes are not mutually exclusive across years, and I would want the committee to compare B047 and B006 directly on that criterion.

responses.point: Boppart ranks B006 second, behind the labour-demand candidate. He treats collateral constraints as the core amplification mechanism of macro-finance, and he warns of overlap with the 2022 prize, of the Bernanke link to the accelerator, and of Gertler's appearance on the New Keynesian ballot, which could split recognition.
responses.response: I take the overlap warning seriously and share it. I would answer it by what the citation covers. It should name collateral constraints and balance-sheet frictions and exclude bank runs and deposit-insurance themes, which the 2022 prize addressed. On the split with B048, Gertler's New Keynesian work is largely a different contribution, estimated DSGE and monetary transmission, and a prize on B006 would not pre-empt that ballot. The competing prize is not a reason to withhold credit for a distinct achievement. Boppart's ranking of the labour-demand work first is a fair alternative, and I rank it below B006 mainly because its credit is spread across two strands, tasks and trade shocks, and across the Katz, Dorn and Acemoglu boundaries.

uncertainties: Whether the committee judges B006 sufficiently distinct from the 2022 prize on banks and financial crises, and how much of Gertler's credit is already absorbed by Bernanke's recognition.
Whether three names dilute the clean Kiyotaki-Moore attribution I preferred at the opening stage, and whether Gilchrist's omission is defensible.
How the committee should weigh B047, which I did not rank, against B006 on the common criteria. My expertise does not allow me to judge this reliably.
The empirical status of the specific collateral channel remains mixed. I rely on general knowledge, not independently verified citation or replication data.
statement.conflict_note: No connection to any credited candidate on the shortlist is apparent from my profile. I disclose collegial ties with fellow committee members: I am an IIES colleague of Per Krusell (committee secretary) and Timo Boppart, and I have co-authored with Krusell, Boppart and Richard Friberg. These are not tied to B006, and I disclose them without adjudicating them.
